addresses: A core member is never told that four addresses can already sign in; the page reports a headcount of eleven and silently drops the pending category (visual-desktop, major)
changes.change: The read-only roster card's header gains a second, quieter line under the description, visible at every width: `Outstanding invitations are not listed here.` No count, no addresses, no card. The description `People with a Tally profile.` also stops being `hidden lg:block` on this permission level, so the phone gets the same two-line caveat the laptop does.
changes.rationale: The Invited card the critic asked for is blocked two layers down — `match /invitations/{emailKey}` is `allow get, list: if isAdmin()`, and `TeamPage` already gates the subscription on `can('admin')`, so any read-only rendering of that collection is a denial in the console and an invented number in the UI. That leaves the critic's own fallback, and I took it verbatim in scope: name the category, say nothing about its size. It goes in the card header rather than in a footer under the eleventh row because the defect is a count that reads complete; a caveat that arrives after the reader has already drawn the conclusion has not done its job. It costs 18px of header on the phone and one line on the laptop, where the page had 85px of slack.
changes.breakpoint: both, read-only permission only — the admin page keeps `hidden lg:block` on its description because the Invited card is on screen beside it

addresses: Ten of eleven cells open with the identical string 'Last seen ', which is wider than the datum that follows it; the column has no shape at squint and Hannah's exception has to out-shout ten sentences of comparable length (design-desktop, minor)
Deferred from round 2: does the recency column get a heading?
One column, two ranks — the role outranks the recency on the admin page and the reverse on the read-only one (design-desktop, minor, partially)
changes.change: At table widths the recency cell carries only the value (`11 days ago`), and the constant becomes one small `Last seen` label in the card's existing header band, set on the recency column's left edge. The card header is now the same container-query grid as the rows, so the label lands at x=560 exactly where the values do, with no row inserted between the title and the first person. Below `@2xl` the prefix stays inside the cell and the label is hidden. The `@container` moved from the `<ul>` to the card root so the header participates in the same query. Role and Access get no heading.
changes.rationale: The two critics disagreed and I took the design critic's version, because its argument survives the visual critic's objection and the visual critic's does not survive the design critic's. The visual critic's case for leaving it alone was cost — 'two new label sets plus a responsive prefix' — and that cost was for a header row; a single label in a header band that already exists is one element, one column, and the other two columns keep labelling themselves ('Counselor', 'Active'). The benefit the visual critic priced at zero is not zero: the eye can fixate past a constant prefix when it is reading a cell, but not when it is ranking eleven of them, and 'Never signed in' now stands as the only phrase in a column of bare durations rather than the eleventh sentence of similar length. It also buys the role/recency rank finding for free.

addresses: The one control that marks revoked access is drawn in a colour Tally does not own — rgb(59,59,59) with a rgb(133,133,133) border — and reads as filled rather than empty; the declared `bg-ink-900 border-ink-600` are not landing at all, so nothing predicts what it becomes when the ramp flips (design-phone, minor)
changes.change: `CheckboxField`'s input is drawn instead of delegated: `appearance-none`, `bg-ink-950` with an inset `ring-1 ring-ink-600` unchecked, `checked:bg-brand-500 checked:ring-brand-500` with a white tick as a background image, and a `focus-visible` ring in `brand-400`. The empty state is now a recess in the `ink-900` card with a ramp-coloured edge; the checked state is visually what it already was.
changes.rationale: I declined this twice as a style preference in a shared control. The design critic's framing is different and correct: `border-ink-600 bg-ink-900` are dead classes — a native checkbox is painted by the user agent, so what ships is Chrome's dark-mode control, a warm grey off the ink ramp, and the light theme's answer is whatever Chrome decides rather than whatever `--color-ink-*` flips to. That is a bug in a shared control, not a taste question about one screen, and the cost of fixing it is the thing I was protecting against anyway — `appearance-none` plus a drawn box — which now buys correctness rather than preference. The tick is unchanged, as the critic asked, so the distance between checked and unchecked grows rather than shrinking.
changes.breakpoint: both — it is the same control at both sizes; `size-5` and the 44/36px label target are untouched

Drop `border-ink-600 bg-ink-900 accent-brand-500`. Every checkbox in Tally changes identically and all of them improve.

addresses: The collapse reports a clean 4 when one of the four is switched off — the removal does not hold on round 2's own stated grounds (visual-phone, minor)
The Invited card has no disclosure marker, so it reads as a title bar with a button beside it rather than a closed container; the two card headers are also different heights (design-phone, minor)
The disclosure has no closed-state affordance: the only way back is a control that still reads '＋ Invite someone', which names adding, not closing (visual-phone, minor)
changes.change: Three edits to one summary. (a) The same rotating `▸` the header disclosure uses now leads the `Invited` title below `lg`, so one mark means 'this opens' everywhere on the page. (b) A danger-toned `1 suspended` badge sits under the title while the card is shut, and hides the moment it opens (and at `lg`, where the rows are always visible) — the count says how many, the mark says how many are not live, in the same vocabulary the row uses. (c) The trailing affordance is state-aware: `＋ Invite someone` when closed, `Close` when open. (d) Both card headers put their title block in a `flex min-h-11 flex-col justify-center`, so they settle on one height below `lg`.
changes.rationale: The exception mark went on its own line rather than beside the count because inline it overflows a 390px frame — and it would still overflow on a longer count or a narrower phone, which is exactly the kind of fit that must not depend on the seed. I did not give the open state a different label than 'Close': the marker rotation plus a word that names shutting is the minimum that makes the thing that opened it visibly the thing that shuts it, and anything more is a second mechanism.

addresses: Dana Ruiz's row is the only one not on the table's grid and it breaks it twice: 'Admin' hangs 13px left of the ten select values, and the wrap makes the row 6px taller so the recency floats between two role lines (design-desktop, minor)
changes.change: The self row's role cell is an intentional two-line cell at table widths: `@2xl:flex-col @2xl:items-start @2xl:gap-0 @2xl:pl-3`. `Admin` now starts at x=756, the same optical edge as the select values below it, the note is its own second line instead of the residue of a wrap, and the row is 53px like the other ten. Below `@2xl` the role and note stay inline, which is what the phone already showed.
changes.rationale: The critic offered two shapes and this is the one that keeps the row height: the note fits on one line in the 224px the cell spans, so stacked it is 36px — exactly the height of the identity cell beside it — where inline it wrapped to 52px. The 12px inset is the select's own text offset, not a magic number: it is what makes a static word and a control value share a lane.

addresses: Where a column mixes a badge with plain text, the badge's padding pushes its label ~6px off the column's edge, so both value columns have two left edges — broken precisely on the exception and the elevated roles (design-desktop, minor)

The role lane is set on the box's edge rather than the word's; and a row whose role or recency is a capsule is a few pixels taller than its neighbours, so the divider rhythm wobbles with who happens to be an admin (design-phone, minor)
changes.change: A badge that stands in a column of text is pulled back by its own inline padding on both edges (`-mx-1.5`), so the label owns the lane whichever edge the lane is set on — the left one in the desktop table, the right one in the phone's trailing role slot. And the cells that can hold either a badge or a line of text get `min-h-5`, which is the badge's own height, so no row buys extra height for carrying one. Measured after: all eleven read-only rows now equal, and the eleven admin rows 53px each.
changes.rationale: One rule instead of two: `-mx-1.5` needs no knowledge of which side the column is aligned on, which matters because the same badge sits in a left-aligned grid cell at `@2xl` and a right-aligned flex slot below it. I fixed the height wobble from the text side rather than by flattening the badge — shrinking `Badge`'s line box would thin every badge in the app to fix a 4px rhythm on one screen.

Two class changes, no new structure.

declined.finding: Give the read-only page the admin's two-column grid and a controls-free Invited card (visual-desktop, major, primary fix).
declined.why: Blocked by a product decision already enforced two layers down: `firestore.rules` has `match /invitations/{emailKey} { allow get, list: if isAdmin() }`, and `TeamPage` gates `subscribeInvitations` on `can('admin')` for exactly that reason. A core member's client cannot read the collection, so the card would be a picture of data the browser does not have. Answered with the critic's own fallback instead — one line naming the category, no count, no addresses.

declined.finding: Sticky card headers on the phone, or a trailing-edge treatment for invitation rows that is not the member toggle's twin, because the two lists blur together while the invite card is open (visual-phone, minor).
declined.why: Re-argued on the open frame, which the critic was right that nobody had looked at — I shot it. Open, the invitation list ends at y=1174 and the roster list starts at y=1256, and between them is a card boundary: two 16px gaps, two ring edges, and a 69px header band carrying 'Signed-in team 11'. A thumb does not cross that without passing a title. Within a row the two lists now differ at the leading edge (a 110px role select vs. a `Withdraw` button), at the identity line (a display name vs. a bold address), and — new this round — in the meta line, where an invitation carries a role token and a person does not. Sticky positioning is new scroll machinery for a distinction three row-level cues already make.

declined.finding: Drop the deferred recency header row from the backlog and leave the column as it is; the scan cost of the repeated prefix is close to zero (visual-desktop, minor).
declined.why: Taken the other way — see the recency change and its rationale. Recorded here because the two critics asked for opposite things and the next round should know this was a decision, not an oversight: the label is one element in a header band that already existed, not the header row this critic priced, and the other two columns still label themselves.

declined.finding: Close the rank gap between the role column and the recency column so the pair reads the same way with and without controls (design-desktop, minor).
declined.why: Half done, deliberately. The prefix drop gives the recency the presence a bare value carries, which is the resolution the critic themselves predicted. The other half would mean dimming a select value that round 1 already stripped of its ring at rest, and a control that is neither ringed nor bright reads as inert text — which is worse than a role that outranks a date.

declined.finding: The invitation rows still vary by 2.7px in height because of the badge-carrying meta line.
declined.why: The same `min-h-5` that fixed the roster would push the Invited card's bottom edge from y=893 to y=901 at 1440×900 and clip the card's own border in the fold frame. A 2.7px wobble in a four-row stacked card that no critic raised is not worth a visible cut at the fold.

declined.finding: The two card headers are still 2px apart on the phone (70px vs 68px).
declined.why: The Invited header carries a second line while it is shut — the `1 suspended` mark — and that line is the point. Equalising would mean padding the roster header by 2px to match a state the other card only sometimes has.

declined.finding: Ten solid brand ticks are the most saturated stripe on the page and encode the state that needs no attention (design-desktop, round 2, minor).
declined.why: Now cheap to do — the checkbox is hand-drawn as of this round, so `checked:bg-brand-500` could be any token — and still declined. The one distinction on this page that must never blur is checked from unchecked, and the unchecked box was just moved down the ramp to `ink-950`; stepping the tick down too would close the gap from both sides in the same round. If the stripe still reads loud next round, that is the change to make, and it is now one class.

declined.finding: The banner promises that some admins are pinned by the deployment and no row ever says which (visual-desktop round 1, major).
declined.why: Carried forward unchanged: `TALLY_ADMIN_EMAILS` lives in Functions config and nothing in `users/{id}` tells the browser a given admin is pinned. The fix is a data change first — have the auth trigger write `pinned: true` onto the user document, expose it on `UserProfile`, then treat `member.pinned` as `isSelf` is treated in `TeamPage.tsx`.
